## The first thing to try

**Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Restart session and run all**.

A notebook remembers everything you have ever run, including cells you have since edited or deleted. Restarting clears that memory and runs your cells in the order they appear. 

## Colab problems

### My variables disappeared

The runtime may have disconnected. Try running your cells again from the top.

### It says I cannot save

You may have someone else's notebook open. **File** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Save a copy
in Drive**, then work in your copy.


## Python errors

### `NameError: name 'Auto' is not defined`

The cell that created `Auto` has not run in this session. Try running your workbook from the top to be sure the data has been loaded.

### `KeyError: 'Balance'`

No column by that name. Check the spelling, including capitals:

::: {#0784ff03 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import pandas as pd
DATA = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucyMcGowan/sta-363-f26/main/data/"
Credit = pd.read_csv(DATA + "Credit.csv")
list(Credit.columns)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1}
```
['ID',
 'Income',
 'Limit',
 'Rating',
 'Cards',
 'Age',
 'Education',
 'Gender',
 'Student',
 'Married',
 'Ethnicity',
 'Balance']
```
:::
:::


### `ValueError: Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead`

scikit-learn wants the predictors as a data frame with columns, even when there
is only one.

::: {#dca5f8a8 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
X = Auto["horsepower"]      # wrong, this is one dimensional
X = Auto[["horsepower"]]    # right, note the double brackets
```
:::


### `ValueError: could not convert string to float`

A text column reached a model that only takes numbers. Either drop it or encode
it:

::: {#48e7673d .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
y = (Credit["Student"] == "Yes").astype(int)
```
:::
